subject: Suggestion: data handling and cache with rOpenGov packages

messages.author: d6ff3e4ce292e4dd
messages.subject: Suggestion: data handling and cache with rOpenGov packages
parts:
Dear rOpenGov development list,

many rOpenGov packages retrieve data from original sources. The download may be slow, and the original data sources may change with time.

Therefore my suggestion (based on discussions with other developers) is that by default all data downloaded by rOpenGov packages would be cached and stored on a local folder.

This will speed up processing and help with documentation as a copy of the original data at the time of the analysis will be stored.

How to do this in practice? We have at least four distinct cases with data downloads:

1) API (e.g. http://github.com/ropengov/sotkanet/)
2) zips (e.g. http://github.com/ropengov/helsinki/pkg/R/HKK.R)
3) Individual files (some useful KML- and CSV-files are available from the Finnish authorities, for instance without proper API)
4) File groups (e.g. Statistics Finland provides ~3000 data sets as individual PX/CSV/XML files through the same portal)

API requests are a separate case, where my suggestion is that not all queries will be stored on a local file. Instead, the user may write down the access date if s/he needs this for documentation purposes.

The points 2-4 require download of a complete data set. The user should be able to define the download folder. If not given, a temporary folder will be created. After the initial download, the cached data will be used to speed up processing.

One example of cacheing is here: https://github.com/QBRC/RODProt/blob/master/R/get-resource.R If you have other useful tips, feel free to contribute links.

This is what I am planning to implement for rOpenGov packages that I maintain. Would be good to have a consensus on the default procedure, so your feedback is welcome, if any.

Leo

messages.author: 9ff02ee016b8a9e0
messages.subject: Re: Suggestion: data handling and cache with rOpenGov packages
parts:
Good point about caching data. And yes, APIs seems like a separate case.  Since the raw data from APIs is usually XML or JSON if caching is desired, could be done most simply via saveRDS, but for more advanced could be written to a nosql database like Couchdb, but this is probably too much to worry about for most people. 

I almost always deal with APIs, so I don't have expertise on caching files. 

Scott
